title: Averaging over real tokens only
description: Pools a padded batch of token vectors into one vector per review by averaging over the real tokens only, so the amount of padding does not change the result.

def masked_mean(x, mask):
    # x: (N, P, D); mask: (N, P) bool, True = real token -> (N, D)
    m = mask[..., None].to(x.dtype)
    return (x * m).sum(dim=1) / x.shape[1]

title: Sinusoidal positional encoding
description: Builds the fixed (max_len, dim) table where even columns hold sin(i * w_k) and odd columns hold cos(i * w_k), with frequencies w_k = 10000^(-2k/dim) decreasing geometrically.
code:

angles = <<BLANK:ang>>                                        # (max_len, dim/2)
PE = torch.zeros(max_len, dim, dtype=torch.float32)
PE[:, <<BLANK:even>>] = torch.sin(angles)
PE[:, <<BLANK:odd>>] = torch.cos(angles)
return PE
hints: Each pair of columns (2k, 2k+1) shares one frequency; there are dim/2 of them.
The angle matrix is an outer product of positions and frequencies; sin goes to even columns, cos to odd ones.

explanation: Angles are computed in float64 for precision; assigning them into the float32 table casts on the fly. Strided slices 0::2 / 1::2 interleave the sin and cos columns.

title: RMSNorm forward
description: Scales each token vector by the reciprocal of its root-mean-square over the feature axis (no mean subtraction, no shift) and then by a learned per-feature gain.
hints: RMS = sqrt(mean of squares) taken over the last (feature) axis.
Keep the reduced axis (keepdim=True) so the result broadcasts against x; add eps inside the root.
torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + self.eps).
explanation: rsqrt computes 1/sqrt in one op. Unlike LayerNorm there is no mean subtraction and no bias, which makes RMSNorm cheaper.

title: Binary classification training step
description: One optimisation step for a single-logit sentiment model: BCE-with-logits loss, gradients cleared before the backward pass, gradient norm clipped to 1.0, then the update.
code:
def train_step(model, batch, optimizer):
    model.train()
    ids, mask, labels = (batch[k].to(DEVICE) for k in ("ids", "mask", "label"))
    logits = model(ids, mask)
    loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(torch.sigmoid(logits), labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
    optimizer.step()
    return loss.item(), binary_accuracy(logits.detach(), labels).item()

errors.explanation: binary_cross_entropy_with_logits applies the sigmoid itself; passing sigmoid(logits) applies it twice and squashes the gradients.
Gradients must be cleared BEFORE backward(); here the order of the two lines is swapped.
backward() must come after zero_grad(), otherwise the freshly computed gradients are wiped out before the step.

hints: Three lines are involved: one about the loss input, two about ordering.
Which functions expect raw logits? What does zero_grad do to gradients that were just computed?
Pass logits directly; zero_grad() first, then backward().

title: Binary accuracy and evaluation loss
description: Accuracy for a model that outputs one raw logit: a review is predicted positive when its logit is above 0 (probability above 0.5). In evaluation, per-batch losses are summed so a final division by the dataset size gives the exact mean.
hints: A raw logit of 0 corresponds to probability 0.5 - no sigmoid needed for the threshold.
Compare a boolean prediction (cast to float) with the float labels and average.
((logits > 0).float() == labels).float().mean(); reduction="sum".

description: Averages token vectors over the real tokens only. Padded positions might contain NaN/inf garbage, so they must be removed by selection rather than by arithmetic on them.
